title: "Swiss administrative geometries"
description: "Choose and discover an official boundary product for analysis or mapping."

<div class="toolbox-kind">Resource · verified 2026-10-04</div>

## Product choice

| Product | Prefer it for |
|---|---|
| OFS historized administrative boundaries G1 | Normal spatial analysis and thematic maps around 1:250,000–1:500,000; default choice |
| OFS historized administrative boundaries K4 | Lighter maps around 1:500,000 and smaller scales |
| swissBOUNDARIES3D | Work that genuinely needs much higher geometric precision |

G1 is already generalized; use swissBOUNDARIES3D only when the extra detail serves the analysis. When related layers need additional simplification, process them together so shared topology remains consistent.

## Verified STAC collections

```text
ch.bfs.historisierte-administrative_grenzen_g1
ch.bfs.historisierte-administrative_grenzen_k4
```

Both collections cover historized administrative states from 1850 and are updated annually. They expose dated items plus an archive-wide item. Their current collection extent ends at `2026-01-01`; query the catalog rather than assuming a year is available.

## The short G1/K4 workflow

G1 and K4 are not tile-download workflows. A dated item contains the complete Swiss dataset, so no bbox, polygon search, tile selection or mosaic is needed:

```text
G1 or K4 + date → dated STAC item → one national GPKG → choose a layer
```

Use G1 unless the lighter K4 geometry is specifically useful. Change only `product` and `date` in the examples below.

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
library(here)
library(httr2)
library(sf)

product <- "g1"            # "g1" or "k4"
date <- "2024-01-01"       # municipality state required

collection_id <- paste0(
  "ch.bfs.historisierte-administrative_grenzen_",
  product
)
item_id <- paste0(
  "historisierte-administrative_grenzen_",
  product,
  "_",
  date
)
item_url <- paste0(
  "https://data.geo.admin.ch/api/stac/v1/collections/",
  collection_id,
  "/items/",
  item_id
)

response <- request(item_url) |>
  req_perform()
resp_check_status(response)
item <- resp_body_json(response, simplifyVector = FALSE)

gpkg_assets <- Filter(
  function(asset) identical(
    asset$type,
    "application/geopackage+sqlite3"
  ),
  item$assets
)
stopifnot(length(gpkg_assets) == 1)

raw_dir <- here("input", "raw", "swiss_geometries")
dir.create(raw_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
destination <- file.path(
  raw_dir,
  basename(gpkg_assets[[1]]$href)
)

if (file.exists(destination)) {
  stop("Destination already exists: ", destination)
}

request(gpkg_assets[[1]]$href) |>
  req_perform(path = destination)

layers <- st_layers(destination)
layers

commune_layer <- grep(
  "^Communes_",
  layers$name,
  value = TRUE
)
stopifnot(length(commune_layer) == 1)

sf <- st_read(
  destination,
  layer = commune_layer,
  quiet = TRUE
)
```

### Python

```python
from pathlib import Path

import geopandas as gpd
import requests

product = "g1"             # "g1" or "k4"
date = "2024-01-01"        # municipality state required

collection_id = f"ch.bfs.historisierte-administrative_grenzen_{product}"
item_id = f"historisierte-administrative_grenzen_{product}_{date}"
item_url = (
    "https://data.geo.admin.ch/api/stac/v1/collections/"
    f"{collection_id}/items/{item_id}"
)

response = requests.get(item_url, timeout=30)
response.raise_for_status()
item = response.json()

gpkg_assets = [
    asset
    for asset in item["assets"].values()
    if asset.get("type") == "application/geopackage+sqlite3"
]
if len(gpkg_assets) != 1:
    raise ValueError(f"Expected one GPKG asset, found {len(gpkg_assets)}")

raw_dir = Path("input/raw/swiss_geometries")
raw_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
destination = raw_dir / Path(gpkg_assets[0]["href"]).name

if destination.exists():
    raise FileExistsError(destination)

with requests.get(gpkg_assets[0]["href"], stream=True, timeout=120) as response:
    response.raise_for_status()
    with destination.open("wb") as file:
        for chunk in response.iter_content(chunk_size=1024 * 1024):
            if chunk:
                file.write(chunk)

layers = gpd.list_layers(destination)
print(layers)

commune_layers = layers.loc[
    layers["name"].str.startswith("Communes_"),
    "name",
]
if len(commune_layers) != 1:
    raise ValueError("Expected one municipality layer")

gdf = gpd.read_file(destination, layer=commune_layers.iloc[0])
```
::::

The GPKG contains municipalities, districts, cantons, country and lakes in EPSG:2056. Layer names include the product and date, so inspect them instead of hardcoding one historical layer name. If only one administrative level is needed, the same item also exposes separate GeoJSON assets. Shapefile is available but is not the default.

Use the [generic geo.admin STAC recipe](../recipes/geoadmin-stac.qmd) for tiled products, spatial searches, pagination or unfamiliar collections—not for this normal G1/K4 case.
